items.place: Supreme Court of India, New Delhi
items.headline: Khalid, Imam bail sent to larger bench
items.text: The Supreme Court sought police replies by 14 Dec on bail for Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam, held over six years under UAPA, but refused interim bail until a three-judge bench rules.

photo.alt: A domed red and cream building with an Indian flag, behind trees and a black statue on a pedestal.
photo.caption: The Supreme Court of India in New Delhi, in 2019. File photo.

items.place: Near the Jharkhand Vidhan Sabha, Ranchi, Jharkhand
items.headline: Tree-felling protesters detained near Ranchi Assembly
items.text: Police detained over a dozen people protesting a 10-lane road that a petition says needs about 7,000 trees felled. Police said protests are barred within 1 km of the Assembly.

photo.alt: A wide, empty two-lane road with street lamps and roadside trees under heavy grey clouds.
photo.caption: A road leading into Ranchi from Birsa Munda Airport, in 2018. File photo of the city.

items.place: Great Nicobar Island, Andaman and Nicobar Islands
items.headline: Nicobar forest-rights hearing pushed to January
items.text: The Calcutta High Court gave the Centre until 10 Dec to answer forest-rights challenges to the Great Nicobar project and deferred final hearings to January. The Centre says the Forest Rights Act doesn't apply.

photo.alt: Dense green forest sloping down to a flooded coastal plain with dead tree trunks and the sea under rain.
photo.caption: Rain over forest and coast in the Great Nicobar Biosphere Reserve, seen from a watchtower in 2016. File photo.

items.place: City Civil and Sessions Court, Bengaluru, Karnataka
items.headline: Basava book author, publisher get interim bail
items.text: A Bengaluru court granted interim anticipatory bail on 25 Nov to author Ravi Hanj and publisher Vishweshwar Bhat. Prosecutors said the book insulted Basavanna; police say they are still seizing copies.

photo.alt: A large domed granite government building with columns and an Indian flag, behind a fenced lawn under a cloudy sky.
photo.caption: Vidhana Soudha, seat of Karnataka's government in Bengaluru, in 2019. File photo.

items.headline: Five ASHA protesters taken to hospital
items.text: Rain drenched about 200 ASHA workers on day nine at Freedom Park; five were hospitalised in two days. The CM promised to raise their ₹15,000 demand; they want it in writing.

photo.alt: A curved wooden-slat path between low plants and tall trees in a green park.
photo.caption: A path among the trees at Freedom Park, Bengaluru, in 2024. File photo.

items.place: Ed Damazin and El Roseires, Blue Nile, Sudan
items.headline: Drone strikes on homes kill families
items.text: Drones hit homes in Ed Damazin and El Roseires on 24 Nov, killing at least 16, including 14 from three families, local officials said. They blamed the RSF and SPLM-N; no response was reported.

photo.alt: Rooftops and a tall beige building seen through the branches of a leafy tree under a hazy sky.
photo.caption: A street view in Damazin, capital of Blue Nile state, in 2019. File photo.

items.headline: Strike on Shati flat kills family of four
items.text: An Israeli strike on a Shati camp flat killed a Hamas security official, his wife and daughters aged 15 and 13, Gaza's interior ministry said. Israel's military said it 'eliminated' a 'terrorist'.

photo.alt: Aerial view of a coastal camp reduced to rubble and gutted buildings, with the sea on the right.
photo.caption: Destruction in Beach (Shati) refugee camp, Gaza City, seen from the air in July 2024. File photo.

items.headline: UN rights chief warns of widening atrocity risk
items.text: UN rights chief Volker Türk warned on 25 Nov of a widening risk of atrocity crimes against Palestinians; his office says 42,666 were displaced in the West Bank since Oct 2023. No Israeli response reported.

photo.alt: A metal turnstile and fenced checkpoint with a guard tower, between old stone buildings.
photo.caption: An Israeli checkpoint at Tel Rumeida in Hebron, in 2015. File photo.

items.headline: Police ban march against term-limit change
items.text: Zambian police banned a 25 Nov march by rights groups opposing calls to scrap presidential term limits, citing a rival rally. Organisers appealed; a minister said the president seeks no third term.

photo.alt: A multi-lane road with a minibus and a white car, below a blue-glass tower block rising behind trees.
photo.caption: A main road in Lusaka, Zambia, in 2023. File photo.

items.headline: A year after deadly fire, critics face arrests
items.text: A year after the Wang Fuk Court fire killed 168, HRW says critics were arrested for sedition and memorials curbed. Officials apologised and pledged reform; police say event decisions rest with organisers.

photo.alt: A row of tall brown residential towers behind a waterfront park and trees, with green hills behind.
photo.caption: Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po, Hong Kong, in 2009, years before the fire. File photo.

items.headline: Father says son killed after army arrest
items.text: Two young men arrested by soldiers in Kapoeta on 30 Oct were killed, a father says; their bodies are missing. The army says they were freed that night; the governor's office is following up.

items.headline: South Sudan orders free movement for campaigners
items.text: President Salva Kiir ordered forces on 25 Nov not to arrest or harass candidates and campaigners for lawful activity, after parties complained of travel curbs. Campaigning runs 27 Dec to 9 Feb.

photo.alt: A wide view over low-rise buildings and tin roofs of a city stretching to a hazy horizon.
photo.caption: Juba, South Sudan's capital, seen from above in 2018. File photo.

focus.title: Sudan's long war
focus.dek: Drone strikes on homes in Ed Damazin and El Roseires killed at least 16 people on 24 Nov, Blue Nile officials and residents said.
focus.alt: Women in long robes and headscarves walk across sandy ground carrying bags and boxes of supplies on their heads and in their arms, with more people behind them.
